set.summary: Three days after the Coastal Road attack Israel invaded southern Lebanon against PLO bases and within days occupied the south up to the Litani River, except Tyre and its surroundings. On 15 March Lebanon protested to the Security Council that it had no connection with the commando raid, reporting that an undetermined number of Lebanese citizens had been killed, notably in Tyre, and that large numbers of people were fleeing the south. On 19 March the Security Council (resolution 425) called on Israel to withdraw and created UNIFIL. Published tolls for Lebanese and Palestinian dead differ: Middle East Eye gives around 1,000 (most of them civilians), Jewish Currents 1,000 to 2,000, the Lebanese government (in a UN document) 1,168 killed in seven days, and MERIP over 2,000 civilian deaths; Jewish Currents and MERIP both put the displaced at about 200,000. By 19 March the IDF spokesman reported 18 Israeli soldiers killed, and two Israeli civilians were killed by shelling and rocket fire in the Galilee (about 20 Israeli dead in all); Chief of Staff Gur estimated about 300 guerrillas killed, not counting those killed by air, artillery and naval fire, while MERIP reports about 100 Palestinian guerrillas killed.

affected_populations.note: IDF spokesman, total since 15 March as reported on 19 March 1978 (JTA, 20 Mar 1978); Middle East Eye also gives 18 Israeli soldiers.

Estimates differ: IDF Chief of Staff Mordechai Gur about 300, excluding those killed by air, artillery and naval attacks (JTA, 20 Mar 1978); MERIP (1982) about 100 Palestinian guerrillas.

Totals of Lebanese and Palestinian dead, civilians and fighters not separated in most sources: Middle East Eye around 1,000, most of them civilians; Jewish Currents 1,000 to 2,000 (including some Palestinians); Lebanese government (UN document, 1998) 1,168 killed in seven days; MERIP over 2,000 Lebanese and Palestinian civilian deaths, above the upper end of this range. Displaced: Jewish Currents some 200,000 displaced or made homeless; MERIP over 200,000 refugees. Lebanon's own letter to the Security Council (S/12600, 15 Mar 1978) gave no number: 'an undetermined number of Lebanese citizens were killed, notably in Tyre'.

set.summary: Eight Israeli F-16s escorted by F-15s destroyed the Osirak (Tammuz) research reactor, under construction by French technicians near Baghdad, on 7 June 1981. Israel said the reactor would have become operational within months and could produce nuclear weapons; Labor's Mordechai Gur argued it was not as close to completion as Prime Minister Begin had suggested. The National Security Archive (George Washington University) states that ten Iraqi soldiers and one French engineer were killed; French sources told JTA one French technician was killed, while Israel's communique had said no technicians were on the site. The Security Council unanimously condemned the attack in resolution 487 and the United States briefly suspended F-16 deliveries.

set.summary: After Hezbollah attacks on Israeli forces and rocket fire on northern Israel, the IDF carried out a week-long air and artillery campaign in south Lebanon. Human Rights Watch reports that the Israeli government's stated objective was to create a refugee flow toward Beirut to pressure the Lebanese government to rein in Hezbollah; some 300,000 Lebanese villagers and Palestinian refugees were temporarily displaced. HRW counted some 120 Lebanese civilians killed and close to 500 injured; in Israel two civilians were killed, both in Kiryat Shmona, and 24 injured by Hezbollah rockets, and about half of Kiryat Shmona's residents left the town during the week. Hezbollah fighter deaths are disputed: Hezbollah later told HRW that seventeen of its fighters were killed, the IDF estimated fifty to eighty guerrillas killed, and Lebanese prime minister Hariri said eight. A US-brokered understanding took effect on 31 July.

affected_populations.note: HRW: 'some 120' killed, 'close to 500' injured; some 300,000 villagers and Palestinian refugees temporarily displaced

Figures conflict and are partisan. Hezbollah (to HRW, interview of 20 Oct 1993): seventeen of its fighters killed during the week of 25 July; IDF (Col. Ben-Ari to HRW, 18 May 1994): between fifty and eighty guerrillas killed; Lebanese PM Hariri (Washington Post, 1 Aug 1993): eight Hezbollah fighters killed.
HRW counts Palestinian refugees among the ~300,000 displaced without a separate figure

set.summary: Israel launched a three-week air and ground offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip on 27 December 2008, which ended on 18 January 2009; Palestinian armed groups fired rockets at southern Israel during it. Palestinian deaths: the IDF's March 2009 figure is 1,166 (709 involved in hostilities, 295 uninvolved civilians, 162 undetermined); B'Tselem counted 1,387 (773 who did not take part in hostilities, including 320 minors; 330 combatants; 245 policemen per Ynet's report of B'Tselem's data, 248 in B'Tselem's own release); the Palestinian Center for Human Rights (PCHR) counted 1,434 (960 civilians, 239 police, 235 combatants, as reported by Ynet). The dispute centres partly on the police, whom PCHR counted as non-combatants and an Israeli think tank (ICT) said were often Hamas militants. Palestinian figures cited by the BBC give more than 5,300 injured; 55,000 people sheltered in UN schools at the height of the fighting and at least 66,000 had still not returned home a week after the ceasefire. Thirteen Israelis were killed according to B'Tselem as reported by Ynet: three civilians and a security officer by rocket fire, five soldiers in Gaza and four soldiers by friendly fire. The UN fact-finding mission led by Richard Goldstone, which Israel refused access, reported in September 2009 strong evidence of war crimes and crimes against humanity. On 1 April 2011 Goldstone wrote in the Washington Post that 'If I had known then what I know now, the Goldstone Report would have been a different document', adding that the Israeli investigations would probably have influenced the mission's findings about intentionality and war crimes (as quoted by the Jewish Virtual Library).

More than 5,300 injured (Palestinian figures, BBC). Displaced: 55,000 sheltered in UN schools at the height of the fighting, at least 66,000 not yet home a week after the ceasefire (BBC); no other displacement or homeless figure was opened.

Subset of the Palestinian dead, not additional: 245 per Ynet's report of B'Tselem's data; 248 in B'Tselem's own 9 Sept 2009 release; 239 per PCHR (reported by Ynet). The IDF figures do not give a police count in the sources opened.
